question: A rectangular lawn measures 40 m by 30 m. A 2 m wide path is constructed all around the inside of the lawn. What percentage of the lawn's area is occupied by the path?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a path constructed inside a rectangle = 2w(L + B − 2w)

⇒ Path area = 2 × 2 × (40 + 30 − 4) = 4 × 66 = 264 m²

Total area of the lawn = 40 × 30 = 1200 m²

⇒ Percentage occupied by path = (264 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangular lawn (L) = 40 m

Breadth of the rectangular lawn (B) = 30 m

Width of the inside path (w) = 2 m

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total area of the lawn = 40 × 30 = 1200 m²

⇒ Length of the inner rectangle = 40 − (2 × 2) = 40 − 4 = 36 m

⇒ Breadth of the inner rectangle = 30 − (2 × 2) = 30 − 4 = 26 m

⇒ Area of the inner rectangle = 36 × 26 = 936 m²

⇒ Area of the path = Total area of lawn − Area of the inner rectangle

⇒ Area of the path = 1200 − 936 = 264 m²

⇒ Required percentage = (Area of path ÷ Total area) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (264 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Path Inside a Rectangle

When a path of uniform width *w* is constructed all around the inside of a rectangle of length *L* and breadth *B*, the area of the path = 2w(L + B − 2w).

Path Outside a Rectangle

When a path of uniform width *w* is constructed all around the outside of a rectangle of length *L* and breadth *B*, the area of the path = 2w(L + B + 2w).

Cross Path in the Middle

When two mutually perpendicular paths of uniform width *w* are drawn through the center of a rectangle, parallel to its length and breadth, the area of the paths = w(L + B − w).
